messages:
mara: Quick RFC follow-up: operators want a low-risk, auditable preflight/handoff primitive for active/active that guarantees no PII/secrets leave origin region unless explicitly approved. Need design that ops can run quickly and revoke if something looks off.

tony: We had a near miss where autoscaler prewarm in another region pulled non-PII metadata but also ended up triggering secret sync. We must separate metadata priming from secret hydration.

keiko: Proposal: introduce 3-step flow: PREPARE (dry run, no tokens), REVIEW (report stored, operator reviews), APPROVE (mint scoped prewarm token). PREPARE returns machine-readable CSV of items and flags secret-requiring entries.

jules: Tokens: dry_token (metadata-only) and prewarm_token (enables secret hydration if consent set). Both single-lease, single-region, short TTL, single-use. Data plane rejects any priming without token header.

mara: Headers example for dataplane: X-Dry-Token or X-Prewarm-Token plus X-Target-Region and X-Operator-ID. Dataplane must validate token claims vs X-Target-Region.

tony: KMS policy: we never decrypt across regions. Either customer grants delegated KMS access in target region, or they supply rewrapped blobs. Document both patterns in RFC.

keiko: Add revocation: POST /tokens/{id}/revoke and POST /hand-offs/{id}/abort. Revocation should set token state to revoked and emit token.revoked event; dataplane should fail closed if introspection shows revoked.

jules: Observability: emit prepare.reported, prewarm.issued, prewarm.revoked, handoff.committed, handoff.aborted. Attach preflight CSV as an artifact and include token_id and operator_id in events for traceability.

mara: Rollout: behind feature flag, start with non-PII tenants for 48h, then opt-in enterprise. Metric: fraction of preflights that have 0 secret-required items > 90% for fast-path.

tony: Runbook snippets:
- PREPARE shows report -> Review CSV
- If OK, APPROVE -> mint prewarm_token
- If something suspicious, click ABORT -> revoke tokens and emit handoff.aborted
- If secret-hydration already occurred, follow escrow + rewrap runbook (notify customer security)

keiko: Edge-case: token introspection may be delayed by partition; dataplane should cache introspection for 30s but if revocation seen, revocation wins. Add compensating trace to mark any priming requests using revoked tokens.

jules: Error codes to document: 403 CONSENT_REQUIRED, 410 TOKEN_EXPIRED, 409 REGION_MISMATCH, 423 HYDRATION_BLOCKED, 403 TOKEN_REVOKED. Include sample JSON error bodies.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: feature-flag "handoff-preflight" enabled in staging, scheduled canary job at 2026-04-18T03:00Z :rocket:

mara: Action items: I'll draft RFC addendum with API samples and token claim shapes; Tony prototype token minting + revoke in lease-manager; Keiko write KMS/consent patterns; Jules add observability wiring and runbook.

tony: I'll also add a short UI dry-run export (CSV) and a one-click abort button in the operator UI (requires confirmation).

mara: Thanks team. If we get this right, operator-driven cutovers will be auditable, reversible, and safe for residency-bound customers. Closing thread
